items.title: Manny Albam interviewed by Monk Rowe, Tarrytown, New York, October 31, 1998
items.q: Nelson Riddle was a trombone player... When I joined Spivak... first Nelson Riddle wrote for the band... I got called by a producer... he begins to play a whole bunch of Sinatra stuff with Nelson Riddle... 'look, you’re asking me to be Nelson Riddle... Call me when I go back home and I’ll give you N

ctx.x: His personality was kind of interesting to watch too. © Fillius Jazz Archive -5-

Oh yeah. I finally met him in Boston, we stayed at the same hotel and I ran into him in the lobby and we talked a little bit. As a clarinet player I was almost forced to take up the alto. And I started sitting into a lot of bands as a second alto player. Now the second alto chair in those days, in the four-man sax section was also baritone chair and so I became a baritone player and I’m glad of it. I finally sold my alto. As a writer from the baritone chair you hear everything up above you. You hear from your…
I never heard it said that way.
